item.message: Skill descriptions were shortened to fit the 2% skills context budget. Codex can still see every skill, but some descriptions are shorter. Disable unused skills or plugins to leave more room for the rest.

item.text: {"brief_complete":false,"completion_reason":"Three material workflow-experience decisions remain unresolved: how Work modes share continuity, how workflows are authored, and how users move from originating tabs into canonical run operations.","questions":[{"decision_key":"work_conversation_mode_continuity","label":"Work mode continuity","context":"A conversation is one resumable history with its own saved context. Work will offer Chat, Coding, and Research modes, but the brief does not decide whether a conversation keeps one mode or can change modes while underway","evidence":"`apps/web/app/page.jsx` currently has no Work tab or conversation-mode hierarchy; the verified replacement introduces Chat, Coding, and Research under Work. `packages/contracts/index.mjs` already defines per-run context, while the product brief locks Work memory to each conversation.","impact":"This determines the Work tab's first-screen organization, resume behavior, context assembly, and whether Coding or Research-specific evidence can be interpreted consistently later. It also sets the long-term boundary between a conversation's identity and the tools it may use.","question":"How should Chat, Coding, and Research relate to a resumable Work conversation?","choices":[{"number":1,"text":"One mode per conversation","consequence":"The operator chooses a mode when creating the conversation and resumes it in that mode; changing purpose creates a linked new conversation. This keeps controls and stored context predictable, at the cost of more conversations when work evolves."},{"number":2,"text":"Switch modes in place","consequence":"The operator may change one conversation between Chat, Coding, and Research at any time. This feels flexible immediately, but creates lasting complexity around tool permissions, context interpretation, and mode-specific history."},{"number":3,"text":"Mode-specific branches","consequence":"A conversation begins in one mode and may fork into another mode while retaining an explicit parent link. This preserves provenance and flexibility, but adds branch navigation and comparison concepts to the core Work experience."}],"allow_multiple":false,"recommended_choice":1,"recommendation_reason":"A fixed mode gives each conversation a clear purpose, stable controls, and an auditable context contract. Linked follow-on conversations still support evolving work without making every resumed session ambiguous.","priority":93},{"decision_key":"workflow_authoring_primary_interaction","label":"Workflow authoring model","context":"A workflow stage is one defined step, such as running a model, validating output, or waiting for a person. A dependency states which earlier stages must finish before another can begin. The six-tab plan does not choose a","evidence":"`adapters/runtime-adapters/src/harness-executors.mjs` already executes constrained stages, and `packages/contracts/index.mjs` defines run states including `approval_required`. The new Workflows tab must expose schedules, batches, and multi-agent stage definitions, but `apps/web/app/page.jsx` currently has no workflow-authoring surface.","impact":"This chooses the main authoring mental model and therefore shapes validation, keyboard use, branching visibility, version comparison, and how easily complex workflows remain understandable as NexusCentral grows.","question":"What should be the primary interaction for authoring and reviewing workflow stages?","choices":[{"number":1,"text":"Structured stage list","consequence":"The first screen presents ordered stage cards with dependencies, authority, inputs, and outputs; an optional dependency diagram appears under an advanced view. This makes common workflows fast and accessible, while complex branching is less immediately spatial."},{"number":2,"text":"Visual dependency canvas","consequence":"Stages are primarily created and connected as nodes on a canvas. Branching is visually explicit, but routine editing, keyboard access, responsive layouts, and large-workflow maintenance become more demanding."},{"number":3,"text":"Equal list and canvas modes","consequence":"Every workflow has synchronized list and canvas editors from the start. Operators can choose their preferred representation, but the product must maintain two equally capable editing experiences and resolve cross-view conflicts long term."}],"allow_multiple":false,"recommended_choice":1,"recommendation_reason":"Most stage configuration is structured operational data, so a list keeps the hero workflow direct and supports accessibility and responsive use. A derived diagram can explain complex dependencies without becoming a second source of truth.","priority":91},{"decision_key":"cross_tab_run_navigation","label":"Run navigation","context":"Runs is the authoritative place for immutable execution history, meaning records that cannot be silently rewritten after work starts. A contextual run summary is a small status view shown where work originated, with a","evidence":"`services/nexus-node/src/run-coordinator.mjs` already returns canonical run status, route, result, experiment, and artifact records. `packages/central-client/index.mjs` is the shared command boundary, while the planned tabs assign execution evidence and approvals exclusively to Runs.","impact":"This decides how operators monitor work without duplicating ownership across Work, Router, Models, and Workflows. It changes first-screen density, interruption cost, and whether future clients can preserve one consistent operational model.","question":"How should users move between originating work and the authoritative Runs record?","choices":[{"number":1,"text":"Contextual summaries with deep links","consequence":"Work, Router, Models, and Workflows show only compact status, failure, and completion summaries that open the exact record in Runs. This preserves tab ownership and low clutter, though detailed intervention always requires moving to Runs."},{"number":2,"text":"Global activity drawer","consequence":"A persistent drawer shows active and recent runs from every tab, with links into Runs. Monitoring becomes faster across tasks, but a global control competes with each tab's hero content and adds responsive complexity."},{"number":3,"text":"Runs-only monitoring","consequence":"Originating tabs confirm submission and provide no continuing status beyond a link. Ownership is maximally clear, but operators must repeatedly visit Runs and may lose the connection between configuration and outcome."}],"allow_multiple":false,"recommended_choice":1,"recommendation_reason":"Compact contextual summaries preserve the six single-purpose tabs while keeping status close to the action that created it. Runs remains the sole detailed operational surface, preventing evidence and intervention behavior from fragmenting.","priority":86}]}
